caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 990 of 2022.
lawyer:
ABM Siddiqur Rahman Khan, Advocate, instructed by Md Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. 
Khaled Ahmed, Advocate, instructed by MadhuMalati Chowdhury Barna, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondent No. 2. 
None Represented—For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Nurul Islam Biplob (Md) -------- Petitioner

State and another ----------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Nuruzzaman, J: This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 24-5-2022 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.38738 of 2022 rejecting the application summarily. 

 2. The accused-petitioner filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 38738 of 2022 before the High Court Division arising out of CR Case No.802 of 2020 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, pending in the Court of learned Joint Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Barishal. 

 3. The respondent No.2 herein as complainant lodged the petition of complaint being CR Case. No.802 of 2020 (Sadar) on 23-11-2020 before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Barishal alleging inter alia that, she has a business institution of Rod & Cement namely, "Messrs Milon Trading" in Alekanda Barishal. The accused person used to buy Rod & Cement from the shop for some years and made good relationship with the complainant. Thereafter, from 2-7-2020 to 20-7-2020, the accused-petitioner purchased 2,000 bags cement and submit a cheque amounting to Taka 30,77,347 (Taka thirty lac seventy seven thousand three hundred forty seven) only in favour of "Messrs Milon Trading" being Account No. 0330-1020- 0048-4 and Cheque No. 4595159, Sonali Bank, Shagordi Branch, Barishal. The complainant went to Sonali Bank, Shagordi Branch, Barishal on 20-10-2020 for encashment of the cheque in favour of "Messrs Milon Trading", but, the same was dishonoured as insufficient fund and returned the cheque on the same date. The complainant sent a legal notice on 21-10-2020 requesting the accused-petitioner to give back the money within thirty days, but, he did not pay any heed over this matter. Hence the case. 

 5. Subsequently, the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Barishal transferred the case record to the Court of learned Joint Sessions Judge, Court No.2, Barishal and re-numbered as Sessions Case No.759 of 2021. 

 8. On 25-1-2022, the accused-petitioner filed an application for handwriting expert to examine the handwriting of the amount of cheque money and the date of the cheque. Subsequently, the accused-petitioner filed an application for withdrawing the case from argument to hearing. 

 9. The Trial Court after perusing the record was pleased to call some essential witnesses to the just decision of the case by the order dated 13-3-2022. 

 11. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 21-3-2022 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Barishal in Criminal Revision No.62 of 2022, the accused-petitioner filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.38738 of 2022 before the ligh Court Division in Sessions Case No.759 of 2021 arising out of CR Case No.802 of 2020 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, pending in the Court of learned Joint Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Barishal. 

 14. Mr ABM Siddiqur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioner submits that, the accused-petitioner as complainant filed a petition of complainant being CR Case No.119 of 2022 before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Barishal against complainant under section 406/420/467/468/471/409 of the Penal Code for forgery and increasing the cheque amount which is now pending for hearing before the said Court. The learned Metropolitan Magistrate directed the concerned Officer-in-Charge to investigate the case and submitted the report before the Court. 

 15. As per direction of the Court of Metro-politan Magistrate, the investigating officer took up the case for investigation. After investigation, the Investigating Officer submit-ted an investigation report 10-12-2021 stating that,- 

 16. The revisional powers of the Court of the learned Sessions Judge, Barishal is embodied under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, and the Court of Sessions shall proceed with the same powers as per section 439 of the Code of Criminal procedure. The section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is as "No order under this section shall be made to the prejudice of the accused unless has an opportunity of being heard either personally or by advocate in his own defense". But, in this case, the learned Sessions Judge, Barishal without giving an opportunity to hear the accused-petitioner either personally or by advocate in his own defense allowed the revision directly by the order dated 21-3-,2022 which is a sheer abuse of process of the law which the High Court Division failed to consider the same. He further submits that, the revisional Court without considering the material facts and record of the case reversed the order of the Trial Court, and caused serious miscarriage of justice which the High Court Division failed to consider the same. He finally submits that, the Trial Court may issue summons upon the witnesses or to examine any person in attendance at any stage of the inquiry, trial or other proceedings as per section 540 of the Code Criminal Procedure, if his evidence appears to be essential to the just decision of the case, and accordingly the Trial Court called 7 (seven) witnesses, but, the Revisional Court without considering the material facts and record of the case reversed the order of the Trial Court caused serious miscarriage of justice, but, the High Court Division failed to appreciate the same, and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set-aside. 

 17. Mr Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2 made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division, and, submitted that, it is a case under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881, the trial Court with-drawing from the argument issued summons of 7(seven) witnesses for taking evidence on the extraneous materials. The case of Negotiable Instrument Act, requires witness is the complainant and documentary evidence. But, the trial Court in an omnibus views called 7(seven) witnesses in the case of Negotiable Instrument Act which rightly set-aside by the learned Sessions Judge as well upheld by the High Court Division. He further argues that, the precedents referred by the learned Advocate for the leave petitioner, the facts of the case are quite difference and, as such, do not applicable in this case. Hence, he prays for dismissal of the instant petition. 

 18. On perusal of the instant case record it is found that, on 13-3-2022, the case was fixed for pronouncing judgment and the accused herein the petitioner submitted an application for withdrawing the case from pronouncing judgment to hearing arguments as his engaged learned Advocate couldn't submit arguments on the date fixed. There was no petition for adducing more witnesses from either side on that day. However, the Trial Court, after hearing arguments afresh, in his own motion and without any self-satisfactory reasons fixed the case for trial afresh and summons 7(seven) witnesses by the impugned order which are as follows: 

 20. It reveals that, there was no petition for adducing more witnesses from either side on that day. However, the Trial Court, after hearing arguments afresh, in his own motion and without any self-satisfactory reasons fixed the case for trial summoning seven (7) defence witnesses after moving back the same after hearing arguments instead of fixing a date for pronouncing judgment. We don't find any cogent reasons justifying such suo moto order summoning 7 (seven) witnesses of the learned Joint Sessions Judge of Trial Court in such a belated stage of the case. 

 21. The submission advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in respect of section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not mandatory for the learned Sessions Judge, while he found that, the order of the trial Court is unjust and without any legal authority. He could dispose of the revisional application without admitting the case and notifying the accused persons for further hearing. In the present case, on perusal of all the facts of the case it appears that, the trial Court fixed the case for further evidence without any application on the side of the prosecution or accused. No doubt under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the Court can call for any witness for the ends of justice. However, for passing such order, the trial Court or Court of Appeal below must be given satisfactory reasonings in issuing the summons to the witnesses under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. On perusal of the impugned order dated 13-3-2022 of the trial Court, it appears to us that, the trial Court without giving any cogent reasons or any satisfaction as Court passed the unjust and unreasonable order issuing summons under section 540 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for further evidence of 7(seven) witnesses in a case of Negotiable Instrument Act. In that view of the matter, we are of the considered view that, the revisional Court in setting aside the judgment and order of the trial Court dated 13-3-2022 committed no error of law. Therefore, we find that, in rejecting the application by the High Court Division does not call for any interference by this Division. 

 22. We have gone through the citations referred by the learned Advocate for the leave petitioner. On perusal of the facts of the precedents it appears that, the facts of the present case and the facts of those referred cases are quite distinguishable, and, as such, we are although respectfully agreeing with the principles of those cases, but, unable to apply in the instant case. 

 24. However, for ends of justice, our considered view is that, it will be justified to secure the ends of justice, if an order be passed transferring the case to another competent Court of the same Sessions Division for further argument and judgment. 

 25. The learned Sessions Judge, Barishal is directed to transfer the instant case from the Court of learned Joint Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Barishal to any learned Joint Sessions Judge, Barishal forthwith. The learned Joint Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Barishal is directed to transfer the instant case records to the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Barishal for taking necessary steps in accordance with law.
